_comment: Title-translation settings. Everything the program needs lives here; command-line flags exist only to override a value for a one-off run. Paths may use / or \. Defaults are tuned for the 16 GB RTX 4060 Ti / 26-core / 512 GB box.

paths._comment: input_dir is scanned recursively for .json/.jsonl files. articles_subdir restricts that scan to folders of that name, because each month folder also holds crawler bookkeeping json (progress.json, dns_cache.json, metrics/, logs/) that is not article data; set it to "" to scan everything. The output file is written as output_dir/output_file and doubles as the resume checkpoint.

article_id._comment: The raw article_id restarts numbering in every month folder, so it is prefixed to stay unique: '<prefix><separator><month folder>/<article_id>' -> '2022_01/article_000094047'. prefix 'auto' uses the input_dir folder name when it looks like a year (e.g. .../ssd/2022 -> '2022'); set an explicit string to force one, or "" for none.

fields._comment: Record keys read from each source file. language may be absent - see the language section.
fields.title: title

language._comment: NLLB needs a source language per title. When the language field is missing or unrecognised, the language is detected from the title text itself. langdetect is pure Python and therefore GIL-bound, so detection runs in a pool of worker PROCESSES - on threads it throttles the whole pipeline and leaves the GPU idle. Titles shorter than detect_min_chars, or whose language stays unknown, are copied through unchanged so they remain searchable.

model._comment: Loaded from the local HuggingFace cache (offline). Titles are short, so input/generation length is capped for speed.
model.name: facebook/nllb-200-distilled-1.3B

gpu._comment: Batches are sized by KV-cache budget, not by a fixed count, so short titles pack into far bigger batches than long ones and VRAM stays full either way. A slot = one cached token = decoder_layers*2*d_model*2 bytes = 96 KiB for the 1.3B, so kv_slot_budget 110000 targets ~10.5 GB of KV on top of the ~2.6 GB model, out of 16 GB. max_batch_size is a fragmentation guard, not a throughput knob: it caps the per-decode-step logits buffer (batch x 0.5 MiB). Batches that still overshoot are split automatically on out-of-memory. Raise kv_slot_budget if peak VRAM sits well below ~14 GB; lower it if OOM splits show up in the summary.

cpu._comment: readers = threads parsing the (many, tiny) json files. detect_workers = separate PROCESSES running language detection, the CPU-heavy stage; set near the core count. detect_chunk = titles a reader hands to a detection worker in one round trip.

runtime._comment: translate_chunk = titles pooled and length-sorted before a translation pass; bigger pools pad less and keep the GPU busier. buffer_queue = pools kept ready for the GPU thread, so translation never waits on reading. flush/checkpoint control writer durability. limit stops after roughly that many new articles (null = no limit, use for a quick test run).
